question: The value of \(20\) quarters and \(10\) dimes equals the value of \(10\) quarters and \(n\) dimes. What is \(n?\)
solution:
Remove \(10\) quarters from each collection. The remaining \(n\) dimes must have the same value as \(10\) quarters and \(10\) dimes.

A quarter is worth \(25\) cents and a dime is worth \(10\) cents, so that remaining value is
\[
10\cdot25+10\cdot10=350\text{ cents}.
\]
The number of dimes needed is therefore
\[
n=350\div10=35.
\]
Thus \(n=35\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
